Allystar Technology designs satellite navigation (GNSS) chipsets and modules supporting GPS, BeiDou, GLONASS and Galileo, spun out of a university-linked chipset research group. Its low-power positioning chips and receiver modules are sold to makers of vehicle telematics, wearables, drones, surveying gear, asset trackers and IoT devices, earning revenue from chip and module sales to OEMs. Operates mainly in China with customers across Asia. Privately held, with a large Chinese funding round in 2023. Pure B2B component supplier with essentially no consumer brand awareness, so sponsorship appeal is limited to technology and automotive-electronics audiences.

Andion Global is a waste-to-energy technology provider that builds and operates biogas and biomethane plants, converting organic and food waste, sewage sludge and agricultural residues into renewable gas, electricity and compost through anaerobic digestion. Customers are municipalities, utilities and waste operators, who pay for plant construction, operation and treatment services, while gas and power sales add further revenue. Active mainly in Italy and southern Europe. Part of a group that includes biogas engineering businesses. Private company, B2B and utility oriented, with little public brand awareness; a niche sustainability story rather than a consumer-facing name.

Bravo Natural Resources is a privately held oil and gas exploration and production company that acquires and develops onshore producing properties in the US, with a focus on mid-continent basins such as Oklahoma. It earns revenue by selling crude oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids to midstream purchasers and refiners. The business was financed by private-equity-style capital commitments rather than public markets and is a small-to-mid-sized operator by industry standards. Entirely B2B with no consumer brand; sponsorship interest would be limited to energy-sector corporate hospitality.

Brenco is a Brazilian renewable energy company that, per Crunchbase, implements clean energy projects. It operates in the clean energy and cleantech sectors and is based in Sao Paulo, Brazil. Its name is commonly associated with biofuel and ethanol-linked projects in Brazil, but the input does not confirm specific products, customers or scale. Private company; the funding round dates from 2007. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

DigiCable is an Indian cable television and digital cable network operator, part of the Hathway-era multi-system operator landscape, distributing digital TV channels and set-top box services to households through local cable operators. Revenue comes from subscription fees, carriage and placement fees from broadcasters, and advertising. It operates in the Mumbai region and other Indian cities. Private operator whose funding dates from 2007, an era of cable digitisation in India. B2C subscription service with regional rather than national brand recognition, so limited sponsorship pull beyond local audiences.

Dun & Bradstreet Credibility Corp is a Malibu-based company selling business credit-building and business-funding services to small and medium businesses, built around the Dun & Bradstreet credit data brand under licence and operating as Credibility Capital-style consulting. It helps owners establish business credit profiles, DUNS numbers and access financing. Customers are small business owners, paying subscriptions and service fees. Private firm, B2B and SMB marketing focused, heavily dependent on online advertising. Moderate name recognition through the D&B brand but little independent consumer awareness.

EC Healthcare is a Hong Kong-listed (HKEX: 2138) non-hospital medical services group, running clinics, medical beauty centres, dental, imaging and diagnostic and wellness services under brands such as DR Reborn, Dr Skin, Dr Reborn Dental and Chinese medicine centres. It serves self-paying consumers in Hong Kong, Macau and mainland China, earning revenue from treatments, packages and subscriptions to its medical network. Controlled by founder Dr Tse Jo-ann and Kam family interests, with a large network of outlets. Visible in Hong Kong through retail clinics and advertising, giving solid local consumer brand awareness.

Enefit Green is Estonia-based renewable electricity producer, a subsidiary of state-owned Eesti Energia, operating wind farms, solar parks, hydro, biomass and cogeneration plants across Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and Finland. It sells green power to wholesale markets and retail customers and develops new projects. Listed on Nasdaq Tallinn (EGR1T) since 2021 after an IPO and also listed in Warsaw. Roughly 1+ GW of installed capacity with a growing pipeline. Mostly B2B utility with mid-level brand recognition in the Baltics; the parent Enefit brand is the consumer-facing name.

Interbiak Bizkaia is an organisation based in Bilbao in the Basque Country of Spain. According to the Crunchbase text, its aim is to research, build and conserve infrastructure; the name suggests a link to the provincial government of Bizkaia, a public body for roads and infrastructure, though the input does not confirm this. No industry tags are given. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Modern Wealth Management is an investment advisory firm based in Lenexa, Kansas, in the Kansas City area. Small regional advisor with no known national consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Narragansett Bay Insurance Company is a Rhode Island property and casualty insurer, based in Johnston, writing homeowners and personal lines coverage in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic coastal states. Customers are homeowners buying through independent agents, and revenue comes from premiums and investment income. It was a subsidiary of Narragansett Bay Insurance Holdings and later part of the Pennsylvania-based Cumberland/Maya group of companies via affiliates. Regional personal-lines insurer with moderate awareness among local homeowners and agents, and little national consumer brand presence.

Northern Dynasty Minerals is a Vancouver-based mineral exploration company whose sole major asset is the Pebble copper-gold-molybdenum project in southwest Alaska, held through its Pebble Limited Partnership. The project is one of the largest undeveloped copper-gold deposits in the world but has been blocked by the US Environmental Protection Agency since 2023 over risk to the Bristol Bay salmon fishery. Listed on the TSX (NDM) and NYSE American (NAK). Revenue-free, financed by shareholders and partners, with no consumer brand; mainly known as a controversial environmental case.

Pembroke Resources is an Australian-based energy and resources company, part of the Pembroke group that develops metallurgical (coking) coal mines in Queensland's Bowen Basin, including Olive Downs and the Lake Vermont operations bought from Jellinbah. It sells coking coal to steelmakers in Asia, particularly India, Japan and China. Privately owned and backed by the Pembroke Resources team with institutional investors. Large-scale B2B commodity producer with no consumer visibility, so sponsorship interest would be limited to B2B hospitality.

SiC Processing GmbH is a service provider based in Hirschau in Bavaria that recycles and reprocesses silicon carbide, notably from used wire-saw slurry in solar wafer and semiconductor production, and supplies purified silicon carbide grain for abrasives and technical ceramics. Customers are photovoltaic and wafer manufacturers and industrial abrasive buyers, who pay for recycling services and material. The plant has been tied to the German silicon carbide industry and the Chinese-owned Dongguan-linked wafer chain. Entirely B2B industrial recycler with no public brand awareness.

SolFocus was a US maker of concentrated photovoltaic (CPV) solar systems, using mirrors and lenses to focus sunlight onto high-efficiency cells for utility-scale power plants. Founded in 2005 in Mountain View and later San Jose, it supplied projects in Spain, Greece, Italy, the US and elsewhere and was backed by Russian state-linked Rusnano, Kleiner Perkins and others. It struggled against falling prices of conventional silicon panels and shut down in 2013. B2B equipment supplier with little consumer awareness; no longer operating.

Upper Peninsula Power Company (UPPCO) is a regulated electric utility serving roughly 50,000 homes and businesses across Michigan's Upper Peninsula, with a mix of hydroelectric generation and purchased power, and rates set by the Michigan Public Service Commission. It was long owned by the Wisconsin-based Integrys / WPS group and changed hands in the mid-2010s. Revenue comes from regulated electricity sales to residential, commercial and industrial customers, including mining and paper operations. Strong local recognition in the region but no national consumer brand, and little sponsorship profile beyond community activity.

Vida Health is a San Francisco virtual care company offering digital chronic-condition and mental health programmes that pair members with coaches and clinicians through a mobile app, covering diabetes, hypertension, weight management and behavioural health. It sells mainly to employers and health plans, which pay per-member fees, and also reaches consumers directly. Founded in 2014 and venture-backed, with a late funding round in 2023. B2B2C digital health provider whose brand is known mostly to benefits buyers and plan members rather than the general public.

Adam Aircraft Industries was a Colorado aircraft maker that developed the A500 twin-engine piston aircraft and the A700 AdamJet very light jet, using composite construction. Founded in 2000 by Rick Adam, it delivered a small number of A500 aircraft to private owners and air-taxi operators but ran short of capital and filed for bankruptcy in 2008; its assets were bought by Triton Aerospace. Customers were private buyers and business-aviation operators. Defunct brand, B2B and high-net-worth niche; no active sponsorship relevance.

Adriatic Metals is an exploration and mining company, headquartered in the UK but operating in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where it built the Vares silver-zinc-lead polymetallic mine that started production in 2024 with concentrates sold to smelters. It was listed on the London Stock Exchange (ADT) and the ASX (ADT) and became a takeover target of Dundee Precious Metals, which acquired it in early 2025. Employs several hundred staff locally. B2B commodity producer with no consumer brand; known mainly to investors and mining-sector audiences.

This entry refers to a Liaoning-based duty-free retailer operating under the Zhongchufu name, running tax-free shops for outbound travellers that sell cosmetics, liquor, tobacco, fashion and gifts, with an online e-commerce channel. Customers are international travellers and cross-border shoppers; revenue comes from retail sales. Operations are concentrated in northeast China, and the store count is not confirmed here. Privately held with a large Chinese funding round in 2023. Regional consumer retail name with limited recognition outside northeast China.

Element Power is a London-based developer and owner of wind, solar and storage projects worldwide, founded in 2012 by the former management of Ireland's Airtricity and backed by Hudson Clean Energy and other investors. It develops projects in the US, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific, selling electricity under long-term power contracts to utilities and corporate buyers, and has also sold completed projects to infrastructure funds. A multi-gigawatt pipeline sits behind it. B2B developer with limited public brand awareness.

Hawkwood Energy is a Denver upstream oil and gas company backed by private-equity capital, formed in the mid-2010s to assemble acreage in the Delaware Basin of west Texas and southeast New Mexico. It drills and operates horizontal wells and sells crude oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids to midstream and refining buyers. Privately held, mid-sized operator by US shale standards. Pure B2B energy producer with no consumer profile, so sponsorship relevance is limited to energy-industry corporate hospitality.

IDFC Bank was the commercial bank formed in 2015 from IDFC, India's infrastructure development finance institution, and began retail operations in 2015 with branches and digital banking. It merged with Capital First in December 2018 to become IDFC FIRST Bank, listed on the NSE and BSE, offering savings and current accounts, loans, credit cards and wholesale banking, with a growing retail base of tens of millions of customers. Based in Mumbai. Consumer banking brand with national presence in India and heavy digital marketing.

Magenta Medical is an Israeli medical device company developing Elevate, a miniature heart pump delivered through the leg that supports failing hearts during high-risk procedures and cardiogenic shock. Its catheter-based pump is smaller than comparable devices and has been tested in clinical studies in the US and Europe. Customers would be hospitals and cardiologists buying disposable pump systems. Venture-backed, with a large round in 2024, and a pre-commercial or early-commercial stage. B2B medical technology with no consumer awareness.

Mascoma was a Boston-area biofuel company, spun out of Dartmouth research, developing consolidated bioprocessing microbes to turn non-food biomass such as wood and switchgrass into cellulosic ethanol. It built a demonstration plant in Rome, New York and a commercial-scale project in Michigan, backed by venture capital and the US Department of Energy, and partnered with General Motors. Its yeast technology was taken over by Lallemand in 2015. B2B R&D-stage firm with little consumer visibility; no longer independent.

Moser Baer Solar was the photovoltaic arm of Moser Baer India, the New Delhi group famed for optical disc manufacturing, making crystalline silicon cells and thin-film solar modules in Greater Noida and selling to project developers and distributors. It ran thin-film and cell plants but suffered from falling global solar prices, and the parent Moser Baer entered debt restructuring in 2012. The solar division wound down. Moser Baer was a visible consumer-electronics storage brand in India during the 2000s.

National General Insurance is a Winston-Salem, North Carolina insurer selling personal auto, homeowners, supplemental health and lender-placed insurance through independent agents and online. It was formed by Gary Fink and Robert Stein's holding company National General Holdings, listed on Nasdaq (NGHC) in 2013, and was acquired by Allstate in January 2021 for about 4 billion dollars. It serves millions of policyholders in the US, writing billions in premiums. Mid-profile insurance brand, mostly known through agents.

Novedo is a Stockholm-based group of vertical-market software companies that acquires and develops small and mid-sized Nordic software businesses on a long-term basis, giving them autonomy while sharing capital and know-how. Its holdings serve niches such as property, retail and public-sector software in Sweden, Norway and elsewhere, earning subscription and licence revenue. Founded in the late 2010s, it is private and backed by investors including Danish and Swedish funds. B2B holding company with almost no consumer brand awareness.

Petra Nova is the carbon capture project at the W.A. Parish coal plant near Houston, a joint venture of NRG Energy and JX Nippon Oil & Gas Exploration. Started in 2017, it captured about 1.4 million tonnes of CO2 a year and piped it for enhanced oil recovery at the West Ranch field, funded partly by the US Department of Energy. Operations were mothballed in 2020 and restarted in 2023. Industrial project entity rather than a consumer brand, with little sponsorship relevance outside energy and climate circles.

Quippo Infrastructure Equipment is a Kolkata-based equipment rental company, part of the Quippo group, renting cranes, earth movers, drilling and power gear to construction, infrastructure and oil and gas firms in India. Revenue comes from rental and fleet services, with equipment leased by project contractors. It raised capital from private-equity investors in the late 2000s. B2B industrial services business with no consumer visibility; sponsorship value limited to local infrastructure and engineering circles.

Sif Group is a Dutch manufacturer of XXL monopile foundations and transition pieces for offshore wind farms, with a large production site at Maasvlakte, Rotterdam and a historic steel-structures plant in Roermond. Founded in the 1940s, it delivers foundations to developers such as Orsted and Vattenfall under large project contracts and employs well over a thousand people. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam. B2B heavy industry, well known within the offshore wind sector but not to consumers.

Solvay Specialty Polymers is the high-performance plastics business of Belgian chemicals group Solvay, producing sulfone polymers, polyamides, fluoropolymers such as Halar and Tecnoflon, and Ryton PPS, used in aerospace, electronics, automotive, healthcare and batteries. It has plants across Europe, the US and Asia and sells engineered materials to manufacturers. Sold as a separate business after Solvay's 2023 split, with the specialty chemicals group now branded Syensqo, while Alpharetta, Georgia is its US base. B2B materials brand with no consumer recognition.

Terminus is an Atlanta-based account-based marketing platform that helps B2B companies identify target accounts, run advertising, email and chat campaigns, and measure pipeline across the buying journey. Founded in 2013, it sells subscriptions to marketing and sales teams at software and services firms, and acquired Sigstr, an email-signature marketing tool, in 2021. Venture-backed. Enterprise SaaS with a name known to marketers but no consumer awareness.

Wolf Minerals was an Australian-listed tungsten and tin developer that built the Drakelands mine, also known as Hemerdon, in Devon, England, the largest tungsten deposit in Europe. Its Perth-based management ran an ASX and AIM listing, commissioning the plant in 2015 but struggling with processing recoveries and low prices. It entered administration in 2018 and the mine was sold to Tungsten West. Industrial commodity producer with no consumer profile.

Cascade Bancorp was the Bend, Oregon holding company for Bank of the Cascades, a community bank with roughly 30 branches across central and western Oregon and Idaho, serving small businesses and households with deposits, commercial real estate and consumer lending. Hit hard by the 2008 financial crisis, it recapitalised with a 177 million dollar equity raise led by Anchorage Capital in 2011. It was acquired by First Interstate BancSystem in 2017. Regional bank with local brand awareness only.

Anchor BanCorp Wisconsin was the Madison holding company for AnchorBank, a savings bank with around 60 branches, offering retail and commercial banking, mortgage lending and wealth services across Wisconsin. Damaged by the credit crisis, it received federal assistance, recapitalised in 2013 and listed on Nasdaq (ABCW) before being acquired by Old National Bancorp in 2016. Customers were local households and small businesses. Regional community bank with state-level brand recognition, not a national name.

ClearEdge Power was an Oregon fuel cell company making stationary phosphoric acid fuel cells for commercial buildings and homes, producing electricity and heat on site, with backing from venture investors and a 2013 acquisition of UTC Power's fuel cell business. It had a significant manufacturing base in South Windsor, Connecticut and Hillsboro, Oregon. After burning through capital it went bankrupt in 2014 and assets were bought by South Korea's Doosan. B2B product with no consumer brand; defunct.

ConnectRN is a Waltham, Massachusetts healthcare staffing technology company with a marketplace app connecting nurses and allied health professionals to per-diem, travel and permanent shifts at hospitals and care facilities. Employers pay fees for filled shifts and workforce-management tools, while clinicians pick up flexible work. Founded in 2015 and venture-backed. Covers thousands of facilities across the US. B2B2C healthcare staffing brand known mainly to nurses and hospital HR teams.

Digifi Korea, as referenced by Crunchbase, is a South Korean satellite communications and information technology company based in Seoul, providing maritime and remote-area connectivity services. Customers are shipping fleets, energy companies and enterprises needing satellite broadband, paying subscription and equipment fees. Private firm, B2B focus. Little consumer brand awareness; any sponsorship appeal would lie in shipping and offshore industry networks.

Doctor Anywhere is a Singapore telehealth company, founded in 2017, with an app for video consultations, medicine delivery, health screening, vaccinations and corporate wellness across Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam, the Philippines and Thailand. It earns from consultation fees, pharmacy sales and employer and insurer contracts, and has partnered with large regional insurers and banks. Raised a Series C of around 70 million dollars in 2021 and further funding later. Consumer-facing digital health brand with solid awareness in Singapore and Southeast Asia.

Gaelectric was an Irish renewable energy developer based in Dublin that built wind farms in Ireland and Northern Ireland and developed compressed-air energy storage and flexible gas-fired grid-balancing projects. It sold power from its wind assets to utilities and into the Irish electricity market, and sold stakes in operating wind farms to infrastructure investors. Founded in the 2000s, it was privately held and later wound down as its assets were disposed of. B2B project developer without consumer brand recognition.

Jet is a technology-driven natural resources company based in Boulder, Colorado, according to Crunchbase. It is categorised under mining and mining technology, suggesting a business that applies data or software to exploration or extraction of minerals or energy resources. The input does not confirm its products, projects, customers or scale. Private company with a funding round in 2023. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

L-3 Global Communications Solutions was a unit of US defence contractor L-3 Communications, based in Victor, New York, working in broadcasting and communications equipment and services for government and commercial customers. It operated within the satellite and telecom products side of L-3 and was funded through the parent rather than as a standalone firm. L-3 merged with Harris in 2019 to form L3Harris Technologies. B2B and defence supplier, with strong parent recognition in defence but little consumer awareness.

NSL Renewable Power is a Hyderabad-based Indian independent power producer, part of the NSL Group, developing and operating biomass, hydro, wind and solar plants that sell electricity to state utilities and industrial customers under power purchase agreements. Backed by private investors including a large round in 2014. Mid-sized regional operator with capacity in the low hundreds of megawatts. B2B utility player with little consumer brand awareness.

Photonex is a UK trade show and conference for photonics, lasers, optics and imaging technology, held annually at venues in England, where exhibitors and visiting engineers meet. Revenue comes from exhibitor stands, visitor registration and sponsorships. It is run by the UK photonics industry body Photonics Leadership Group and exhibition organisers, with a technical seminar programme. B2B event with a small, specialist audience of engineers and researchers; no consumer profile.

Tripod Preclinical Research is a Nanjing-based contract research organisation (CRO) offering preclinical services, including animal-model pharmacology, toxicology and drug-metabolism studies, to Chinese and global pharma and biotech clients. It earns fees per study and runs animal-facility and laboratory space in Jiangsu. Funded by Chinese venture and healthcare investors with a large round in 2023. B2B life-science service provider with no consumer visibility.

VitAG is a South Carolina company converting municipal biosolids and other organic waste into pellet fertiliser and bioenergy products, operating a plant at Beech Island near Augusta. Municipal wastewater utilities pay disposal fees, and VitAG sells the finished fertiliser to farmers and landscapers. Backed by private equity and venture-style investment of about 170 million dollars. B2B environmental services firm with niche industry recognition and no consumer profile.

Vytalize Health is a Hoboken, New Jersey company building accountable care organisations (ACOs) for independent physicians, supplying data, care coordination and value-based care infrastructure under Medicare programmes. It combines technology and population-health services to cut hospital spending and shares savings with doctors. Founded in 2017 and venture-backed. Serves practices across the US with a Medicare focus. B2B healthcare services brand known to physicians; patients rarely know it.

Furie Operating Alaska is a League City, Texas-based oil and gas operator that drilled and installed the Julius R. platform on the Kitchen Lights Unit in Alaska's Cook Inlet, the first new offshore platform there in decades, aimed at supplying natural gas to local utilities and industrial users. It was backed by private capital, entered bankruptcy in 2016, and its Cook Inlet assets were taken over by Hilcorp. B2B energy producer with no consumer brand.

Geosign is an internet media company based in Guelph, Ontario, Canada, focused on online publishing according to Crunchbase, where it is classed under internet and publishing. The input does not confirm its sites, products or customers, though the funding date of 2007 suggests it operated in the web-portal era and likely earned revenue from online advertising. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Hospitales MAC is a private hospital operator in Puebla, Mexico, offering medical, surgical and specialist care, diagnostic imaging and emergency services to insured and self-paying patients. Revenue comes from patient fees and insurer payments. It raised a sizeable round in 2023 to expand facilities. Regional healthcare brand with recognition in Puebla and central Mexico; sponsorship use limited to local health-awareness campaigns.

Killick Aerospace is a Dallas-based aviation company supplying commercial engine and aircraft parts and offering aircraft and engine leasing, trading and professional aerospace services. Its customers are airlines, lessors and maintenance providers worldwide, and it earns from parts sales, lease income and service fees. Privately held and mid-sized. Pure B2B aerospace supplier with no consumer profile, though it is known within aircraft-trading circles.

Northstar Aerospace was a Canadian-listed (TSX) maker of helicopter and aircraft transmission components, gears and drive systems, with plants in Milton, Ontario, Bedford Park, Illinois and in the UK. It supplied helicopter makers such as Sikorsky and Boeing and defence customers on long-term programmes. The company entered creditor protection in 2012 and its operations were sold off, so it no longer exists as an independent brand. B2B only, with no consumer awareness and no current sponsorship relevance.

Amonix was a Seal Beach, California maker of high-concentration photovoltaic (HCPV) solar trackers using Fresnel lenses to focus sunlight on multi-junction cells, for utility-scale power plants. Backed by Kleiner Perkins and other investors, it supplied projects including a large plant in Alamosa, Colorado. It was acquired by Arzon Solar in 2013 and ceased operating in 2015 after weak demand. B2B equipment maker with no consumer brand; defunct.

Black Swan Energy is a Calgary oil and gas producer focused on the Montney formation in northeast British Columbia, developing liquids-rich gas and selling oil, gas and NGLs to Canadian marketers. Backed by private equity, it was acquired by Tourmaline Oil in 2021 for roughly 1 billion Canadian dollars. Employed a small team and ran horizontal drilling programmes at Ring Border and Gordondale. Pure B2B energy producer without consumer brand.

Cambridge Technology Partners was a Massachusetts IT consulting and systems-integration firm founded in 1991, known for fixed-time, fixed-price application development for banks, telecoms and corporate clients. It went public on Nasdaq in 1993, grew to thousands of consultants in offices worldwide and was bought by Novell in 2001 for roughly 266 million dollars. Defunct as an independent brand, with no sponsorship relevance today.

Envisics is a Milton Keynes UK company developing dynamic holographic head-up displays for cars, projecting large 3D augmented reality navigation and driver-assist graphics on the windscreen. Founded around 2014 by Cambridge researchers and backed by Hyundai Mobis, Jaguar Land Rover, Sony and others, it licenses technology and supplies modules to carmakers and tier-one suppliers. Its tech first appeared in Cadillac vehicles. B2B automotive technology with little consumer awareness.

Foundation 9 Entertainment was an Irvine, California video game developer group formed in 2006 that owned a collection of independent studios, including Backbone Entertainment, Sproing and Digital Eclipse, producing console, mobile and handheld games for publishers. Revenue came from work-for-hire development and its own titles. Backed by private investors. Studios were later sold or closed and the group declined by the 2010s. Industry B2B brand with limited consumer recognition.

Galloping Horse is an advertising, film and television production company based in Beijing, China, according to Crunchbase. It sits in the advertising and film production sectors and likely makes commercials, drama series and films, though the input does not confirm titles, customers or scale. Private, with a funding round in 2011. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Harmony Energy Income Trust is a London Stock Exchange-listed investment trust, with an address in Knaresborough, North Yorkshire, that owns commercial-scale battery energy storage systems in Great Britain, including Pillswood in Yorkshire and Tynemouth in the north-east, managed by Harmony Energy Advisors. It earns revenue from grid balancing services, wholesale trading and capacity contracts and pays dividends to shareholders. Investor-focused vehicle with no consumer profile, so sponsorship interest is minimal.

HighFive Healthcare is a Homewood, Alabama dental support organisation that acquires and partners with independent dental practices, centralising back-office functions such as billing, procurement, HR and marketing so dentists can focus on patients. It is backed by private equity and healthcare investors and operates numerous practices across the southern US. Revenue comes from the practices' patient fees and insurance reimbursements. Consumer exposure is only through local practice names.

Kernel is a Culver City, California neurotechnology company founded by Bryan Johnson, building non-invasive brain-measurement headsets, Kernel Flow using time-domain functional near-infrared spectroscopy and Kernel Flux using magnetoencephalography. It sells devices and data services to researchers, pharma firms and brain-health programmes. Johnson funded much of the roughly 150 million dollars raised. Known mainly through Bryan Johnson's public profile, with high niche interest among technology audiences.

MAGIX is a Berlin-based software maker known for video, audio and photo editing tools including Vegas Pro, Samplitude, Music Maker, Movie Edit Pro and Sound Forge, sold to consumers, hobbyists and professionals. Founded in 1993, it earns revenue from software licences, subscriptions and downloads, mainly in Germany, wider Europe and the US, and has acquired brands such as Sony's creative software line. Private and investor-owned. Well known among creative software users and hobby video makers, with little mainstream brand profile.

Marin Clean Energy (now MCE) is a California community choice aggregator, a not-for-profit public agency based in San Rafael that buys electricity for customers in Marin, Napa, Contra Costa and Solano counties, offering a higher renewable content than the incumbent utility PG&E. Founded in 2010 as the state's first such programme, it serves over a million customers and earns revenue from energy sales. Public-agency brand with strong local consumer recognition.

Mayapada Hospital is a private hospital network in Jakarta, Indonesia, operated by Mayapada Healthcare Group, with hospitals in Jakarta, Bogor, Surabaya, Bandung and other cities offering oncology, cardiac, neurology and general medicine. Part of the Mayapada group of Dato Sri Tahir, which also includes Bank Mayapada. Revenue comes from patient fees and insurers. It is a recognised premium private hospital brand among Indonesian urban consumers and has been active in marketing.

NextRoll is a San Francisco marketing technology company, parent of AdRoll, the retargeting and ad-platform business, and RollWorks, an account-based marketing platform. It sells advertising software and services to e-commerce brands, B2B marketers and agencies worldwide, charging platform fees and ad-spend commissions. Founded in 2007 as AdRoll, it is venture-backed and has several hundred staff. Well known to digital marketers but not to the general public.

Noah Medical is a San Carlos, California medical robotics company with the Galaxy System, a robotic bronchoscopy platform using integrated tomosynthesis imaging to find and biopsy small lung nodules for earlier cancer diagnosis. Founded in 2018 by Jian Zhang and others, it is venture-backed, with investors including Johnson & Johnson Innovation, and sells systems and disposable scopes to hospitals. B2B medtech with strong awareness among pulmonologists and no consumer profile.

Orchard Street Investment Management is a London-based real estate investment manager focused on UK and European commercial property, including logistics, offices, retail and living sectors. It manages funds and segregated mandates for institutional and pension investors, earning management and performance fees on several billion pounds of assets. Employee-owned alongside institutional backers. B2B asset manager with limited public recognition, though the buildings it owns are visible to tenants and local communities.

Partners Life is a New Zealand life insurer founded in 2010, selling life, trauma, income protection and health cover through independent financial advisers rather than directly to the public. It has grown into one of the country's leading life insurers by new business, with annual premiums above a billion New Zealand dollars and strong adviser ratings. Auckland-based and privately owned. Well known to advisers, less so to consumers, though it has sponsored sports and community events.

Quaero is an interactive media and entertainment business based in Paris, France, per Crunchbase, listed under digital media and marketing. The name is also associated with a large French-German research programme on multimedia search, but the input does not confirm which entity this is, nor its products, customers or scale. Funding dates from 2008. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Tejas Networks is a Bangalore-based maker of optical transport, broadband access and 4G/5G radio networking equipment, selling to telecom operators and government networks in India and emerging markets. A subsidiary of the Tata Group via Panatone Finvest, it is listed on the NSE and BSE (TEJASNET) since 2017 and acquired Saankhya Labs in 2022. It has won large Indian BharatNet and BSNL contracts. Revenue is in the tens of billions of rupees. B2B only, little consumer awareness.

The Healing Company is a New York company that, per Crunchbase, offers conventional and alternative medicine, classed under alternative medicine. It appears to be a consumer health and wellness business, but the input does not confirm which products, brands, clinics or acquisitions it holds, nor its customers or scale. Private, with a large funding round recorded in 2023. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Virtual Benefits Administrator (VBA) is a Milwaukee, Wisconsin provider of cloud-based claims administration and benefits software for employers, third-party administrators and health plans, handling health, dental and self-funded plan claims. It earns software subscription and administrative service fees. Backed by private equity and growth investors with a large round in 2023. B2B healthcare administration firm, known to benefits buyers and brokers but not to the public.

XO is a private aviation company based in Fort Lauderdale offering jet charter, jet cards and membership on a marketplace of operators, plus a fleet of its own Citation jets, to wealthy individuals and corporate flyers. Founded in 2009 as XOJET, it bought Vistajet's US business in 2016 and was acquired by Vista Global in 2020, becoming part of the Vista group. Its customers are US-based, flying thousands of destinations. Recognisable luxury aviation brand with sports and event partnerships.

Dynavox Group, formerly Tobii Dynavox and spun off from Tobii and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm in 2021, makes assistive technology: eye-gaze devices, speech-generating tablets and communication software for people with ALS, cerebral palsy, autism or stroke.
