Losses led to Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2023, and assets were sold. Customers were dermatologists and hospitals. B2B pharma brand with no consumer profile.

CinCor Pharma was a Boston clinical-stage cardiovascular biotech, listed on Nasdaq (CINC), developing baxdrostat, a selective aldosterone synthase inhibitor for resistant hypertension. AstraZeneca acquired it in 2023 for up to 1.8 billion dollars. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer awareness.

Gotham Greens is a Brooklyn-based greenhouse farming company that grows lettuce, herbs, leafy greens and tomatoes in high-tech hydroponic rooftop and large greenhouses across the US, and sells under the Gotham Greens brand in grocery stores like Whole Foods and Walmart, plus dressings, dips and pizza. Founded in 2009, it has around 15 greenhouses in many states. Consumer food brand with growing national shelf presence.

Jubilant Pharma is the pharmaceutical arm of India's Jubilant Bhartia Group, with a US presence at Yardley, Pennsylvania. It runs radiopharmacies, contract development and manufacturing (Jubilant HollisterStier allergy products and Jubilant Radiopharma), generics and active ingredients, serving hospitals, pharma and drug distributors. Revenue is over 1 billion dollars. Parent Jubilant is listed in India. B2B pharma supplier with niche brand recognition.

Little Leaf Farms is a Devens, Massachusetts controlled-environment agriculture company that grows baby lettuce and leafy greens in large greenhouses using rainwater and sells them in clamshell packs in supermarkets across the Northeast and beyond. Founded in 2015 by Paul Sellew, it has expanded to several large greenhouses in Massachusetts and Pennsylvania. Consumer produce brand with solid regional shelf presence and growing national reach.

Marinus Pharmaceuticals was a Radnor, Pennsylvania and Branford, Connecticut biotech, listed on Nasdaq (MRNS), that sold Ztalmy (ganaxolone), approved for seizures in CDKL5 deficiency disorder, a rare epilepsy. Revenue came from the sale to neurologists via specialty pharmacies. Struggling finances led to its acquisition by Immedica Pharma in 2025. B2B pharma brand with no consumer profile.

Quotient Biodiagnostics was a Newtown, Pennsylvania and Edinburgh-based diagnostics company, listed on Nasdaq (QTNT), developing the MosaiQ platform for blood grouping and transfusion testing, with customers in hospitals and blood banks. It struggled with debt and filed for Chapter 11 in 2023. B2B medical diagnostics brand with no consumer profile.

RayzeBio was a San Diego clinical-stage biotech developing radiopharmaceutical cancer therapies that deliver radioactive isotopes such as actinium-225 to tumours using targeting molecules, with lead candidate RYZ101. It listed on Nasdaq (RYZB) in 2023 and was acquired by Bristol Myers Squibb in early 2024 for about 4.1 billion dollars. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer profile.

Standard BioTools, formerly Fluidigm, is a South San Francisco life science tools company, listed on Nasdaq (LAB), selling mass cytometry (CyTOF), microfluidics and proteomics instruments and reagents to academic, pharma and clinical researchers. It merged with SomaLogic in 2024 and sells the SomaScan proteomics platform. Revenue is about 170 million dollars. B2B research tools brand known in labs but not by consumers.

VectivBio was a Basel-based clinical-stage biotech, listed on Nasdaq (VECT), developing apraglutide, a long-acting GLP-2 analogue for short bowel syndrome patients dependent on intravenous nutrition. Ironwood Pharmaceuticals acquired it in 2023 for about 1 billion dollars. Pre-revenue rare disease developer with no consumer profile.

Avistone Pharmaceuticals is a Beijing-based clinical-stage biotech developing targeted cancer therapies, including vebreltinib, a MET inhibitor licensed with Apollomics, and other kinase inhibitors for non-small cell lung cancer. It is private and funded by Chinese and international investors. No marketed products at the time. B2B pharma developer with no consumer profile.

BioRay Pharmaceutical is a biopharmaceutical company based in Taizhou, Jiangsu, China, per Crunchbase, in biopharma and biotechnology. It states it is committed to delivering life-changing medicines, which points to drug development, but the input does not confirm its products, pipeline or customers. Funding of about 2.5 billion yuan was recorded in January 2023. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

California Water Service Group, based in San Jose, is a regulated water utility holding company listed on the NYSE (CWT), supplying water and wastewater services to roughly 2 million people through subsidiaries in California, Washington, New Mexico, Hawaii and Texas. Revenue is around 1 billion dollars, set by state utility commissions. Founded in 1926 and one of the largest US investor-owned water utilities. Utility with strong local recognition but little national brand profile.

eFishery is a Bandung, Indonesia aquaculture technology company, founded in 2013, whose smart feeders and marketplace help fish and shrimp farmers manage feeding, financing and sales across Indonesia and Southeast Asia. It raised 200 million dollars in 2023 at a valuation above 1 billion dollars from investors including Temasek and SoftBank, but in December 2024 an audit found inflated revenue and profit figures, leading to the CEO's removal and a collapse in credibility. B2B agtech with strong local farmer recognition.

Inozyme Pharma was a Boston clinical-stage rare disease biotech, listed on Nasdaq (INZY), developing INZ-701, an enzyme replacement therapy for ENPP1 deficiency and ABCC6 deficiency, which cause calcification and bone disorders. BioMarin agreed to acquire it in 2025. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer profile and not relevant to consumer sponsorship.

KAP Industrial Holdings, now simply KAP, is a South African diversified industrial group listed on the JSE, with divisions that include PG Bison (wood panels), Safripol (polymers), Unitrans (logistics and fuel haulage), Optix (automotive and rubber components) and Restonic and Sleepmasters (bedding). It supplies manufacturers, retailers and consumers in southern Africa. Revenue is about 15 billion rand. Mixed B2B and consumer brands, with Restonic and Sleepmasters well known in South Africa.

PhenomeX was a Emeryville, California life sciences tools company formed in 2023 by the merger of Berkeley Lights and IsoPlexis, selling Beacon and IsoLight single-cell analysis platforms to pharma and academic labs for antibody and cell therapy discovery. It listed on Nasdaq (CELL) and was acquired by Bruker in 2023 for about 600 million dollars. B2B research tools brand with no consumer profile.

Selecta Biosciences was a Watertown, Massachusetts biotech, listed on Nasdaq (SELB), developing ImmTOR tolerogenic nanoparticles to prevent anti-drug antibodies, notably SEL-212 for chronic refractory gout, licensed to Sobi. It merged with Cartesian Therapeutics in 2023 and renamed itself Cartesian Therapeutics, now focused on mRNA CAR-T cell therapy for autoimmune disease. B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

Thrive Earlier Detection was a Cambridge, Massachusetts cancer screening company that developed CancerSEEK, a multi-cancer blood test combining DNA mutations and protein biomarkers, developed with Johns Hopkins researchers and backed by Third Rock and Casdin. Exact Sciences acquired it in January 2021 for about 2.15 billion dollars. Customers were physicians and health systems. B2B diagnostics brand that is now part of Exact.

Ventus Therapeutics is a Waltham, Massachusetts and South San Francisco biotech developing oral small molecule drugs for inflammatory diseases, notably NLRP3 inhibitors for cardiovascular and neurological conditions, using structure-based computational design. It has a partnership with Novartis, which paid an upfront sum in 2022, and is venture-backed. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer profile.

Zhongxin Breeding is a Guangzhou-based Chinese pig breeding service provider, supplying breeding pigs, semen and genetic improvement services to hog farms, and is classed under agriculture and livestock technology. It serves commercial pig farms across southern China, earning revenue from breeding stock and genetics sales. Recorded funding of about 2.4 billion yuan in March 2023. B2B agriculture supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

2seventy bio was a Cambridge, Massachusetts cell therapy company spun out of bluebird bio in 2021, listed on Nasdaq (TYO), which co-commercialised Abecma, a BCMA CAR-T therapy for multiple myeloma, with Bristol Myers Squibb. Bristol Myers Squibb acquired it in 2025 for about 286 million dollars. Customers were cancer centres. B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

Amolyt Pharma was a Lyon-area French biotech, based in Ecully, developing eneboparatide for hypoparathyroidism and other peptides for endocrine and rare diseases. AstraZeneca's Alexion unit acquired it in 2024 for up to 1.05 billion dollars. Pre-revenue developer with no consumer profile.

Amphastar Pharmaceuticals is a Rancho Cucamonga, California specialty pharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (AMPH), making and selling injectables and inhalation products, including enoxaparin, Primatene Mist (an over-the-counter asthma inhaler), naloxone, glucagon, epinephrine and insulin products. It sells to hospitals, wholesalers and pharmacies, with revenue of roughly 700 million dollars. Primatene Mist gives it some consumer recognition in the US.

Atlas Agro is a Zug, Switzerland agricultural technology company developing a way to make nitrate-based nitrogen fertiliser from air, water and renewable electricity, producing it locally in an emission-free process instead of the carbon-intensive ammonia route. Customers would be farmers and agricultural cooperatives buying low-carbon fertiliser. It has raised venture funding and is building first plants. Pre-commercial B2B firm with no consumer profile, but a strong sustainability and climate narrative.

Bluepha is a Beijing synthetic biology and materials company founded in 2016, producing PHA (polyhydroxyalkanoates), a family of biodegradable plastics made by microbial fermentation, as well as other bio-based materials such as ingredients for personal care. Customers are packaging, consumer goods and textile brands, and it runs large fermentation capacity in China. Venture-backed with a large round in 2023. B2B materials firm with growing industry awareness and no consumer brand.

BOCOM International is the Hong Kong-listed (3329) overseas investment banking arm of Bank of Communications, one of China's big banks, offering equity and debt underwriting, brokerage, asset management, research and advisory for Chinese and international institutional and retail clients. It is based in Hong Kong and has a majority shareholder in the state-owned bank. Revenue comes from fees, commissions and trading. Financial services brand with limited consumer awareness outside Hong Kong.

CanSino Biologics is a Tianjin-based Chinese vaccine company, listed in Hong Kong (6185) and on Shanghai's STAR Market, best known for Convidecia, a single-dose adenovirus-vector COVID-19 vaccine developed with the Academy of Military Medical Sciences, and for meningococcal conjugate vaccines such as Menhycia. It sells to national and provincial disease control centres and also supplies partners abroad. Founded in 2009. B2B vaccine maker with high profile in China during the pandemic.

Caribou Biosciences is a Berkeley, California clinical-stage biotech, listed on Nasdaq (CRBU), co-founded by CRISPR pioneer Jennifer Doudna, developing off-the-shelf allogeneic CAR-T cell therapies for blood cancers using chromosome-engineered cells, with candidates such as CB-010 for lymphoma. Revenue is limited to collaboration income, including partnerships with AbbVie and Pfizer. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

GRIT Real Estate Income Group is a Mauritius-domiciled property company, listed on the London Stock Exchange and the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, that owns, manages and develops commercial real estate across Africa, including shopping centres and logistics sites in countries such as Mozambique, Zambia, Ghana and Morocco, leased to multinational tenants. Revenue is rental income. B2B landlord with little consumer profile.

Hookipa Pharma is a New York-based clinical-stage biotech, listed on Nasdaq (HOOK), developing arenavirus-based immunotherapies against cancer and infectious diseases, including HB-200 for HPV16-positive head and neck cancer, partnered with Gilead in an HIV programme. It has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

Integra Telecom is a Portland, Oregon-founded telecommunications provider, with a Vancouver, Washington address in Crunchbase, offering fibre, internet, voice and managed network services to businesses and government customers across western US states. It was owned by private equity and expanded by acquiring local carriers. Customers pay monthly service contracts. B2B telecom brand with regional recognition and no consumer profile.

Lyndra Therapeutics is a Watertown, Massachusetts biotech founded from MIT research, developing ultra-long-acting oral capsules that release medicines over days to a week from a star-shaped structure in the stomach, to improve adherence for conditions such as schizophrenia and malaria. It partners with pharma companies and is venture-backed. Pre-commercial B2B firm with no consumer profile.

Omni Conversion Technologies is an Ottawa, Ontario cleantech company developing a gasification process that converts solid waste and biomass into energy, synthetic gas and fuels, marketed for municipalities and industrial waste producers. It raised several hundred million Canadian dollars of financing commitments around 2011. Private or small-listed company in waste-to-energy. B2B and little public awareness.

Opnext was a Fremont, California maker of optical modules and components for telecom and data networks, including 10G, 40G and 100G transceivers sold to network equipment makers. Spun out of Hitachi and listed on Nasdaq (OPXT), it merged with Oclaro in 2012, forming a larger optical components company that was later acquired by Lumentum in 2018. B2B component supplier with no consumer profile.

ReNAgade Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech, launched by Flagship Pioneering, building an RNA and delivery platform for programmable medicines, including mRNA and gene-editing therapies delivered to tissues beyond the liver. Funded with a 300 million dollar launch round and other venture investment, it is pre-commercial and works through partnerships. Developer for pharma customers with no consumer profile and little public awareness.

Sangon Biotech is a Shanghai-based Chinese life sciences supplier of molecular biology reagents, custom DNA oligos, gene synthesis, DNA sequencing and protein services, selling through catalogues and online to universities, research institutes and pharma labs across China. Founded in 1998 and one of the country's larger reagent suppliers. Revenue comes from product sales and services. B2B laboratory brand known to researchers, with no consumer profile.

SunGard was a Wayne, Pennsylvania financial software and IT services company supplying trading, risk, banking, insurance and availability services to banks, asset managers and corporations worldwide. Founded in 1983, it was taken private in 2005 by a group of private equity firms in an 11.3 billion dollar buyout, spun off its availability business in 2014, and was acquired by Fidelity National Information Services in 2015 for about 9.1 billion dollars. B2B brand known to financial institutions.

Synthekine is a Menlo Park, California biotech developing engineered cytokine therapies that direct immune signalling, using synthetic cytokine receptors to treat cancer and autoimmune diseases, with partners including Roche. Venture-backed with late-stage private funding rounds. Pre-commercial B2B drug developer with no consumer profile.

Tianhe Chemicals Group is a Chinese fluorochemicals producer, based in Jinzhou, Liaoning, making refrigerants, hydrofluoric acid and other fluorine chemicals sold to industrial customers in refrigeration, electronics and chemicals. It was listed in Hong Kong. Revenue depends on commodity and chemical prices. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand.

Unity Biotechnology is a South San Francisco biotech, listed on Nasdaq (UBX), that developed senolytic drugs to clear senescent cells for age-related diseases, with a lead programme in eye disease, UBX1325, for diabetic macular oedema. Co-founded by Nathaniel David and backed by Amazon's Jeff Bezos among investors. It wound down in 2025 after trial results. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with some interest in longevity circles.

US LEC was a Charlotte, North Carolina competitive local exchange carrier, listed on Nasdaq (CLEC), selling voice, data and internet services to small and medium businesses across the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic. It merged with PAETEC Holding in 2007, forming a larger competitive telecom provider that was later bought by Windstream in 2011. B2B telecom brand with regional recognition.

VYNE Therapeutics, formerly Menlo Therapeutics after its merger with Foamix Pharmaceuticals, is a Bridgewater, New Jersey biotech listed on Nasdaq (VYNE). It sold topical dermatology products such as Amzeeq and Zilxi, then sold them to Journey Medical in 2022 and refocused on BET inhibitors for immuno-inflammatory diseases. Small-cap specialty pharma that is now a clinical-stage developer with limited public awareness.

Acepodia is an Alameda, California clinical-stage biotech developing antibody-cell conjugation, which attaches antibodies to the surface of immune cells such as gamma delta T and NK cells to create off-the-shelf cancer therapies without genetic engineering. It was founded in Taiwan and is venture-backed. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Aeglea BioTherapeutics was an Austin, Texas clinical-stage biotech, listed on Nasdaq (AGLE), that developed engineered enzymes for rare metabolic diseases, including pegzilarginase for arginase 1 deficiency. In 2023 it restructured and renamed itself Spyre Therapeutics, now a Waltham company developing antibodies for inflammatory bowel disease. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

AmplifyBio is a West Jefferson, Ohio contract development and testing organisation for cell and gene therapies, providing preclinical safety and efficacy studies, GMP manufacturing, analytical development and clinical-stage services to biotech clients. Its Ohio campus was built for advanced therapy development, with additional capabilities elsewhere in the US. Revenue comes from service fees from developers. Venture-backed B2B life sciences services brand with no consumer profile.

Black Diamond Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts precision oncology company, listed on Nasdaq (BDTX), developing MasterKey therapies against families of oncogenic mutations in EGFR and HER2, with lead candidate silevertinib in glioblastoma and lung cancer. It has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

Boundless Bio is a San Diego precision oncology company, listed on Nasdaq (BOLD), developing therapies against tumours driven by extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), with candidates such as BBI-355, a CHK1 inhibitor, and BBI-825. It has no marketed products and relies on equity funding. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

Campaign Monitor is an email marketing platform founded in Sydney in 2004, used by agencies, marketers and small businesses to design, send and track email campaigns with templates and automation. Insight Partners invested about 250 million dollars in 2014, and the business later became part of CM Group, now known as Marigold, with a US base in Nashville. Revenue comes from subscriptions. B2B software with strong awareness among marketers and no consumer profile.

CardioFocus is a Marlborough, Massachusetts medical device company that makes the HeartLight endoscopic ablation system, a laser balloon catheter used to treat atrial fibrillation with direct visualisation of the heart tissue. It sells to hospitals and electrophysiologists in the US and Europe and is venture-funded. B2B medtech brand known among cardiologists, with no consumer profile.

Chroma Medicine was a Boston epigenetic editing biotech, founded in 2021 by Nessan Bermingham and backed by Flagship Pioneering, developing technology that switches genes on and off without changing DNA. In 2024 it merged with Nvelop Therapeutics to form nChroma Bio. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Eurofarma is a Brazilian multinational pharmaceutical company, based in Itapevi near Sao Paulo, one of Brazil's largest, selling prescription, generic and over-the-counter medicines, plus consumer health and dermocosmetics, in Brazil and across Latin America, with a growing US presence. It was founded in 1972, is privately held by the Lazar family, and has around 10,000 staff. Consumer health brands give it good awareness in Brazil.

Finnforel is a Finnish fish farm that grows, processes and supplies rainbow trout, using land-based and sea-based production in Finland and supplying retailers and food service with fresh and processed fillets. It is headquartered in Helsinki and has attracted large private investment to expand capacity. B2B food producer with growing domestic brand recognition but limited international consumer awareness.

Harpoon Therapeutics was a South San Francisco biotech, listed on Nasdaq (HARP), developing TriTAC T-cell engagers for cancer, including HPN328 for small cell lung cancer, with AbbVie as a partner. Merck acquired it in early 2024 for about 680 million dollars. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

Mariana Oncology was a Watertown, Massachusetts radiopharmaceutical biotech founded in 2021, developing targeted radioligand therapies for cancer, backed by Dimension, Pfizer Ventures and others. Novartis acquired it in 2024 for up to 1 billion dollars. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Mural Oncology is a Waltham, Massachusetts biotech spun out of Alkermes in 2023 and listed on Nasdaq (MURA), developing nemvaleukin alfa, an engineered interleukin-2 therapy for ovarian cancer. After a disappointing late-stage trial in 2024 it moved to wind down its programmes. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

Omega Therapeutics was a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech, listed on Nasdaq (OMGA), founded by Flagship Pioneering, developing epigenomic controllers to programme gene expression for cancer and other diseases. It entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy in early 2025 after financing difficulties. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Orbital Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech developing circular RNA and in vivo cell therapy treatments, aimed at autoimmune diseases and cancer using novel RNA technology with lipid delivery. It was launched in 2022 with Atlas Venture and Dimension investment, and Bristol Myers Squibb agreed to acquire it in 2025 for about 1.5 billion dollars. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Recro Pharma was a Malvern, Pennsylvania pharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (REPH), that ran a contract development and manufacturing business for drug makers and developed Anjeso, an injectable pain drug. It renamed itself Societal CDMO in 2022 and was acquired by CoreRx in 2024. B2B pharma services brand with no consumer profile.

Relievant Medsystems is a Minneapolis medical device company that makes the Intracept system, which uses radiofrequency ablation of the basivertebral nerve inside vertebrae to treat chronic vertebrogenic low back pain. It sells to spine surgeons and pain physicians, with Medicare coverage. Boston Scientific agreed to acquire it in 2024 for about 850 million dollars. B2B medtech brand with no consumer profile.

Ring Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotech launched by Flagship Pioneering, working on anelloviruses, harmless human viruses, as vectors for delivering gene therapies and redosable genetic medicines. It is venture-backed and pre-commercial, with a large funding round in 2023. B2B developer for pharma and patients, with no consumer profile.

Septerna is a South San Francisco biotech, listed on Nasdaq (SEPN) since 2024, building a platform for discovering oral small-molecule drugs against GPCR drug targets, with partnerships with Novo Nordisk, Vertex and Otsuka and lead programmes in endocrine conditions such as hypoparathyroidism. Revenue comes from collaborations. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

Silo is a Fresno, California software and financing company for the produce and food supply chain, providing inventory, order, logistics and payment tools that help growers, packers and distributors manage fresh food and access credit. Customers are food suppliers and distributors in the US, and it raised venture money in 2023. B2B food-tech platform with industry recognition among produce suppliers but none among consumers.

SinoTau Pharmaceutical is a Beijing-based Chinese company, classified in biotechnology and health care, which describes itself as a total solution provider in the field of radiopharmaceuticals for diagnosis and therapy, including PET tracers and nuclear medicine products. It sells to hospitals and imaging centres in China and raised a 1.98 billion yuan round in 2023. B2B healthcare firm with no consumer profile.

Stemirna Therapeutics is a Shanghai biotech focused on mRNA technology, developing mRNA drugs and vaccines, including a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine candidate, with lipid nanoparticle delivery and a production base in Shanghai. Founded in 2016, it raised about 1.7 billion yuan in 2023 from Chinese investors. Pre-commercial or early-stage B2B pharma developer with no consumer profile.

Tessa Therapeutics is a Singapore biotech developing cell therapies for cancer, mainly an EBV-specific CD30 CAR-T treatment for relapsed lymphoma and virus-specific T-cell therapies, with trials in Asia and the US. Founded in 2011, it is venture-backed and runs a manufacturing facility in Singapore. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Vapotherm is an Exeter, New Hampshire medical device company that makes high velocity nasal insufflation systems, Precision Flow and Vapotherm Oxygen Assist Module, delivering heated, humidified respiratory support to patients with breathing difficulty in hospitals, emergency care and home care. It was listed on the NYSE (VAPO) and was taken private in 2024 by lender Perceptive Advisors. B2B medtech brand with strong recognition among respiratory therapists.

10 Biotech is a clinical-stage biotech company based in Copenhagen, Denmark, per Crunchbase, in biotechnology and health care. The description is cut off after saying it is developing therapies, and the input does not confirm its pipeline, indications or ownership. A funding round of about 242 million dollars is recorded in September 2025. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Acrivon Therapeutics is a Watertown and Cambridge, Massachusetts oncology biotech, listed on Nasdaq (ACRV), using its AP3 proteomics platform to match drugs to patients' tumours, with lead candidate ACR-368, a CHK1/2 inhibitor for endometrial and ovarian cancers. It has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

Agile Therapeutics is a Princeton, New Jersey women's health company, listed on Nasdaq (AGRX), that sells Twirla, a weekly contraceptive skin patch, to women in the US through prescriptions, with telehealth and retail pharmacy channels. Revenue is small, around 20 million dollars, and the company has repeatedly raised funds. Consumer-facing prescription brand with limited public awareness.

Alira Health is a Framingham, Massachusetts international advisory and consulting firm for the healthcare and life sciences industry, offering clinical research, regulatory, market access, digital health and strategy services to medtech, pharma and digital health clients, plus its Alira Health clinical research subsidiaries. It has offices across the US, Europe and Asia. Revenue comes from fees. B2B consultancy with brand recognition in the health industry only.

Alterome Therapeutics is a San Diego precision oncology biotech developing targeted small-molecule drugs, including AKT inhibitors for cancers with specific mutations, such as breast cancer, built by a team with prior kinase drug development experience. It has raised venture funding from institutional investors. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

BigCommerce is an Austin, Texas software-as-a-service e-commerce platform, listed on Nasdaq (BIGC), enabling merchants and brands such as Ben & Jerry's, Skullcandy and Burrow to build online stores, B2B portals and multi-channel selling. Founded in 2009, it earns subscription and payment fees from tens of thousands of merchants, with revenue around 330 million dollars. Rebranded as Commerce in 2025. B2B tech brand known among online retailers.

Bluejay Therapeutics is a privately held South San Francisco biopharmaceutical company developing antibody treatments for chronic hepatitis D and other liver diseases, with a lead candidate in clinical trials. It is backed by venture investors and has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Bright Peak Therapeutics is a Basel, Switzerland and San Diego biotech developing immunocytokines, targeted cytokine therapies that deliver IL-2 and other immune signals to tumours, for cancer immunotherapy. It is private and venture-backed, with a funding round in 2024. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

e-Rewards was a Plano, Texas market research company that ran a large online consumer panel in which members earned rewards for taking surveys, selling insights to brands and agencies. It was renamed Research Now in 2011 and later merged with SSI to form Dynata, a global first-party data and research firm. Customers were corporations and research agencies. B2B data brand with some consumer panel recognition.

Effector Therapeutics is a San Diego clinical-stage oncology biotech, listed on Nasdaq (EFTR), developing small molecule translation regulators, including tomivosertib (eFT508), a MNK1/2 inhibitor in combination with checkpoint inhibitors. It has no marketed products and has cut operations. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Engrail Therapeutics is a San Diego biotech founded in 2019 that develops medicines for neuropsychiatric diseases such as anxiety and depression, including GABA-A and other targeted compounds in clinical development. It is venture-backed and private. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

ENTREC was a Spruce Grove, Alberta provider of heavy lift, heavy haul and crane services for oil sands, pipelines, power generation and infrastructure projects, with a fleet of cranes and trailers across western Canada. It was listed on the TSX before being acquired. Customers were industrial and energy contractors. B2B industrial services brand with regional recognition among project managers.

First Water is an Icelandic land-based aquaculture company, based in Thorlakshofn and registered in Kopavogur, farming Atlantic salmon in closed tanks on geothermal land with access to renewable energy. It is expanding to large annual production capacity and sells fresh salmon to retail and food service buyers. Backed by large private investment. B2B food producer with growing European market recognition.

IASO Biotherapeutics is a Shanghai-based cell therapy company with a Nanjing manufacturing base, developing CAR-T treatments for blood cancers and autoimmune disease, including equecabtagene autoleucel (Fucaso), a BCMA CAR-T approved in China for multiple myeloma, plus a US-based clinical arm. It is venture-backed. B2B pharma developer with no consumer profile.

IDRx was a Cambridge, Massachusetts precision oncology biotech focused on gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GIST), developing next-generation KIT kinase inhibitors for patients who relapse on standard drugs. GSK acquired it in 2024 for about 1.15 billion dollars upfront. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

IRIS Software Group is a UK business software company, with an address in Slough, offering accounting, payroll, HR, education and professional services software to accountants, schools and small and mid-sized employers, with products such as IRIS Payroll and IRIS Accountancy Suite. Founded in 1991, it serves around 100,000 customers and is owned by Leonard Green & Partners and Hg-affiliated funds. B2B software with strong recognition among UK accountants.

MBX Biosciences is a Carmel, Indiana biotech, listed on Nasdaq (MBX) since 2024, developing precision peptide therapies for endocrine and metabolic disorders, including MBX 2109 for hypoparathyroidism and MBX 1416 for post-bariatric hypoglycaemia, using its Precision Endocrine Peptide platform. It has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

One Kings Lane is a home decor and furniture e-commerce company, founded in San Francisco in 2009 and later run from New York, that sold designer furniture, rugs, lighting and accessories through flash sales and a marketplace, with brand deals and designers. Venture-backed with Kleiner and others, it was acquired by Bed Bath & Beyond in 2016 and then sold on. Consumer online brand with solid US awareness among home shoppers.

ProfoundBio was a Woodinville, Washington and Suzhou, China biotech developing next-generation antibody-drug conjugates for cancer, including rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S) for ovarian cancer. Genmab acquired it in 2024 for about 1.8 billion dollars. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Rallybio is a New Haven, Connecticut biotech, listed on Nasdaq (RLYB), developing treatments for rare diseases in fetal and neonatal health, including RLYB212 to prevent fetal and neonatal alloimmune thrombocytopenia and RLYB116 for complement-mediated disease. It has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Recipharm is a Stockholm-headquartered pharmaceutical contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO), producing medicines for drug owners with sterile, oral, inhaled and biologics capacity across Europe, the US and Asia. It was listed on Nasdaq Stockholm and taken private by EQT in 2021, and has about 9,000 staff. Customers include global pharma and biotech. B2B manufacturer with no consumer profile.

Rostelecom is Russia's largest integrated digital services provider and state-linked telecom operator, based in Moscow and listed on the Moscow Exchange (RTKM), providing broadband, pay TV, fixed telephony, mobile services through Tele2 Russia, and data centres and cloud, to households, businesses and government. It serves tens of millions of customers with annual revenue of around 800 billion roubles. Major consumer brand in Russia but under Western sanctions.

Seismic Therapeutic is a Watertown, Massachusetts biotech using machine learning to design biologic drugs for immune-mediated diseases, such as engineered enzymes and antibodies for autoimmune conditions. It is venture-backed and has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Shenzhen Luye is the Shenzhen-based arm of Luye Pharma, a Chinese multinational pharmaceutical group that develops and sells drugs for central nervous system disorders, oncology, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, including the Rykindo long-acting antipsychotic injection. The group is listed in Hong Kong. Customers are hospitals and pharmacies in China and abroad. Large funding round of 1.6 billion yuan in 2024. B2B pharma brand with some recognition in China.

Signavio was a Berlin-founded business process management software company, with an address in Walldorf in the Crunchbase record, whose cloud platform let enterprises model, analyse, automate and govern processes. SAP acquired it in 2021 for about 1.2 billion dollars, making it part of SAP Signavio. Customers were large enterprises. B2B software brand known to process and digital transformation teams.

Simcere Pharmaceutical is a Nanjing-based Chinese drugmaker, listed in Hong Kong (2096), with products in oncology, neurology and autoimmune disease, including the stroke drug butylphthalide (Enbipu), the cancer drug Endostar and a pipeline of antibodies and small molecules. It sells to hospitals across China and partners with international biotechs. Founded in 1995, with revenue of over 6 billion yuan. B2B pharma brand with strong hospital recognition in China.

Sinovent is a life sciences technology and development company in Suzhou, Jiangsu, China, per Crunchbase, in biotechnology and life sciences. The input does not confirm what it develops, its customers or ownership. A funding record of about 1.7 billion yuan dates from February 2024. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

TaylorMade Golf is a Carlsbad, California maker of golf clubs, balls and equipment, with drivers, irons, putters and the TP5 ball, sold through golf retailers, pro shops and online to golfers worldwide. Founded in 1979, it was owned by Adidas until 2017 and is now owned by KPS Capital Partners. Its tour staff includes Rory McIlroy, and it is a prominent golf sponsor. Very strong consumer brand visibility in golf.

Wataniya Palestine Mobile Telecommunications is a Palestinian mobile network operator, launched in 2009 in the West Bank and Gaza as a subsidiary of Qatar's Ooredoo Group, with brand Wataniya Mobile, later rebranded Ooredoo Palestine. It provides prepaid and postpaid mobile voice and data to consumers and businesses. Funding of 225 million dollars was raised in 2009 for the licence and network. Well known consumer telecom brand in Palestine.

Aikucun is a Shanghai-based Chinese social e-commerce company that lets individual sellers, many of them stay-at-home parents, resell fashion, beauty, household goods and groceries through WeChat, with the company providing supply chain, fulfilment and customer service. Founded in the late 2010s, it recorded a 2018 funding round and grew to millions of sellers. Consumer-facing app brand with strong reach in lower-tier Chinese cities.

Allgeier is a Munich-based German IT services and software group, listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (AEI), providing digital transformation, software development and consulting to public authorities, banks, insurers and industrial companies through its Enterprise IT and mgm technology partners units. It has thousands of employees and revenue of around 450 million euros. Founded in 1977. B2B IT services brand known in German enterprise and public sector markets.

Aquafin is a company based in Elkton, Maryland, per Crunchbase, in advanced materials and commercial products. The description says only that it entered an exclusive licence agreement, and the input does not say what technology or products it covers. Funding of 200 million dollars is recorded in February 2017. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Asher Bio is a South San Francisco clinical-stage biotech developing cis-targeted immunotherapies, which direct immune-activating cytokines to specific T cells in tumours, with lead candidate AB248 for solid tumours. It is venture-backed and has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Autobahn Therapeutics is a San Diego clinical-stage biotech developing restorative treatments for neurological and psychiatric diseases, based on thyroid hormone receptor beta agonists that aim to promote remyelination in conditions such as multiple sclerosis and adrenoleukodystrophy. It is venture-backed. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Clearside Biomedical is an Alpharetta, Georgia ophthalmic biopharma company, listed on Nasdaq (CLSD), whose SCS Microinjector enables suprachoroidal delivery of drugs to the back of the eye. Its triamcinolone product Xipere is marketed by Bausch + Lomb for macular oedema in uveitis, and it develops CLS-AX for wet age-related macular degeneration. Revenue is mainly royalties and licence fees. B2B pharma brand with no consumer profile.

FIRE1 is a Dublin-based Irish medical technology company developing a device to monitor patients with heart failure from within the body, aimed at managing fluid pressure and improving outcomes for patients with chronic heart conditions. It is venture-backed and pre-commercial. B2B medtech developer with no consumer profile.

Fortress Biotech is a New York and Miami-area holding company, listed on Nasdaq (FBIO), that builds biopharma companies, including Mustang Bio, Journey Medical, Checkpoint Therapeutics and Avenue Therapeutics, and earns revenue from the marketed dermatology products at Journey and royalties. Founded by Lindsay Rosenwald. B2B healthcare holding company with no consumer profile.

Galectin Therapeutics is a Norcross, Georgia biotech, listed on Nasdaq (GALT), developing belapectin, a galectin-3 inhibitor, for patients with advanced fatty-liver cirrhosis (MASH cirrhosis) and for cancer immunotherapy. It has no marketed products and is funded by equity raises. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

Halda Therapeutics is a New Haven, Connecticut biotech developing oral cancer drugs based on regulated induced proximity targeting chimeras (RIPTACs), which kill cancer cells selectively by exploiting differences between tumour and normal cells, led by prostate cancer candidates. Johnson & Johnson agreed to acquire it in 2025 for about 3.05 billion dollars. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

HiBio, Human Immunology Biosciences, was a South San Francisco biotech developing immune-targeted therapies for immune-mediated diseases, such as selective antibodies that address autoimmune and inflammatory conditions. Biogen acquired it in 2024 for about 1.15 billion dollars. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Hibernia Networks, previously Hibernia Atlantic, is a global submarine and terrestrial fibre network operator, with US offices in Summit, New Jersey, that provides bandwidth, IP transit and data services to carriers, enterprises and content companies across the Atlantic and between Europe, the US and Asia. It was bought by Reliance Globalcom in 2007 and became Global Cloud Xchange. B2B telecom infrastructure brand with no consumer profile.

ImCheck Therapeutics was a Marseille, France biotech developing antibodies that activate gamma delta T cells for cancer, with lead candidate ICT01 targeting BTN3A in blood cancers. Ipsen agreed to acquire it in 2025 for an upfront sum of about 350 million euros. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Iterum Therapeutics is a Dublin-based clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (ITRM), developing orally and intravenously administered sulopenem, a penem antibiotic approved in the US in 2024 as Orlynvah for uncomplicated urinary tract infections in women. It has no scale revenue yet. Customers are doctors and pharmacies. Pharma-sector brand with no consumer profile.

LENZ Therapeutics is a San Diego ophthalmic biotech, listed on Nasdaq (LENZ), whose low-dose aceclidine eye drop, approved in the US in 2025 as Vizz, treats presbyopia, the age-related loss of near vision, as a once-daily drop. It sells to eye-care professionals and patients and targets a large market of adults over 40. Consumer-oriented ophthalmic brand in early launch.

Lygos is a Hayward, California specialty chemical company using fermentation and synthetic biology to make bio-based chemicals, such as malonic acid, as a replacement for petroleum-derived ingredients in coatings, adhesives, agriculture and pharmaceuticals. Customers are manufacturers who buy the intermediates. It is venture-backed. B2B chemicals firm with little public awareness.

Molecular Partners is a Swiss clinical-stage biotech, based in Schlieren near Zurich and listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange and Nasdaq (MOLN), developing DARPin protein therapeutics, including radioligand therapies such as MP0712 and T-cell engagers for cancer, with partners like Novartis and Orano Med. It has no marketed products and earns collaboration revenue. Pre-commercial B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

Nuvig Therapeutics is a Menlo Park, California biotech developing immune-modulating therapies for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, using engineered antibody-based drugs. It is private and venture-backed, with a funding round in late 2024. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Penske Media Corporation (PMC) is a Los Angeles digital media and publishing company run by Jay Penske, owning Variety, Rolling Stone, Billboard, Deadline, Hollywood Life, SheKnows, Vibe, Sportico, Robb Report and The Hollywood Reporter. It earns revenue from advertising, events, subscriptions and licensing, with a large global digital audience. Strong consumer media brands and a big events business, giving high visibility to advertisers and sponsors.

Remix Therapeutics is a Watertown, Massachusetts biotech developing small molecules that modulate RNA splicing to treat cancer and other diseases, using a platform that targets pre-mRNA processing. It is venture-backed, with a funding round in 2024. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Sonae Arauco is a leading wood-based panels producer, based in Maia near Porto, Portugal, making MDF, OSB, particleboard and laminate flooring from plants in Portugal, Spain, Germany and South Africa, sold to furniture makers, builders and DIY retailers. It was formed in 2016 when Chile's Arauco forestry group acquired Sonae Industria's panel business. B2B materials supplier with trade recognition and little consumer visibility.

Truvian Sciences is a San Diego diagnostics company developing an automated benchtop blood testing system that runs a broad menu of tests, covering chemistry, immunoassay and haematology, from a few drops of blood in minutes, aimed at clinics and retail health sites. It is venture-backed. Pre-commercial or early B2B medtech with no consumer profile.

Videology was a New York and Baltimore-based video advertising technology company offering a platform that allowed brands, agencies and publishers to plan, buy and manage targeted video ads across TV and digital screens. It raised about 200 million dollars but ran out of funds and filed for bankruptcy in 2018, with its assets sold. B2B ad tech brand known to advertisers, defunct today.

Xiyun International is a Beijing-based group meal catering company supplying canteen and institutional food services to enterprises, schools and organisations, together with brand marketing activity. Customers are employers and institutions who pay for meal service contracts. It raised about 200 million dollars in 2018. B2B food service operator with no consumer brand awareness.

Outpace Bio is a Seattle biotech developing engineered cell therapies for solid tumours, using synthetic biology to improve T-cell persistence and resistance in the tumour environment. It is a spin-out founded with funding from Samsara BioCapital and others, and raised a large round in 2024. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

5Lmeet is a Chinese co-working space and incubator operator, with an address in Shaanxi province according to Crunchbase, which describes it as a co-working space company. The input does not give its locations, member numbers or ownership. A funding record of about 1.19 billion yuan dates from 2018. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Accent Therapeutics is a Lexington, Massachusetts biotech developing small-molecule cancer drugs that target RNA-modifying proteins, such as DHX9 and KIF18A, to treat tumours with specific genetic features. It is venture-backed with a 2024 round and has no marketed products. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Akamis Bio is a clinical-stage oncology company, formerly called PsiOxus Therapeutics, developing tumour-selective viral immunotherapies engineered to deliver cancer-fighting proteins directly inside tumours, with products such as NG-350A. It has operations in the UK and the US and is venture-backed. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

AnaptysBio is a San Diego biotech, listed on Nasdaq (ANAB), that discovers antibody therapeutics, with royalties on GSK's Jemperli (dostarlimab) cancer drug and a pipeline including rosnilimab for rheumatoid arthritis. Revenue comes from royalties and collaboration payments. Founded in 2005. Pre-commercial in its own products, B2B biotech with no consumer profile.

ASLAN Pharmaceuticals is a Singapore-based biotech, listed on Nasdaq (ASLN), developing eblasakimab, an antibody against the IL-13 receptor for atopic dermatitis, after earlier work in oncology with varlitinib. It has no marketed products and is funded by equity raises and licensing. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Attralus is a biopharmaceutical company, based in Naples, Florida and San Francisco, developing therapies and imaging agents for amyloidosis, including pan-amyloid reactive antibodies such as AT-02 and a PET imaging agent, to remove amyloid deposits in the heart and organs. It is venture-backed and pre-commercial. B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Borealis Biosciences is a Vancouver, British Columbia biotech, per Crunchbase, working in biotechnology and life sciences. The description is cut off and says only that it operates in the field of next-generation therapies, and the input does not confirm products or programmes. A funding round of 180 million dollars is recorded in December 2024. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Denovo Biopharma is a privately held San Diego biotech that uses biomarkers to find the patients most likely to respond to a drug, repurposing late-stage and previously failed drug candidates for cancer, neurology and psychiatry, with programmes such as DB102 for lymphoma and DB104 for depression. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Farmers Edge was a Winnipeg digital agriculture company, listed on the TSX (FDGE), providing farmers with satellite imagery, in-field weather stations, field-level analytics and carbon programmes, with millions of acres under subscription across North America, Brazil and Europe. It was taken private by Fairfax Financial in 2023. Customers are farmers, agribusinesses and insurers. B2B agtech brand known among farmers.

Genome Medical is a South San Francisco telehealth company that provides genetic counselling and testing services, with a network of genetic experts available to patients, health systems, employers and health plans. It offers virtual consults, genetic risk assessments and testing with partners. Founded in 2015 and venture-backed. B2B2C health brand with niche recognition in precision medicine.

Group Nine Media was a New York digital media company that owned Thrillist, NowThis, The Dodo, Seeker and PopSugar, producing food, news, animals and lifestyle content for social video audiences and earning revenue from advertising and branded content. It was formed in 2016 and merged with PopSugar in 2019, and later sold off its assets. Strong social video reach, with the Dodo and NowThis having tens of millions of followers.

Groupe Onepoint is a Paris-based French consulting and digital transformation firm, working with banks, insurers, public bodies and large corporates on data, cloud, software and strategy projects, and growing through acquisitions in France, the UK and other countries. It has thousands of employees and revenue of several hundred million euros. B2B consultancy known in French business circles but not to the public.

Grow Up Farms is a London-based urban farming company that raised funding in 2024 to build vertical farms and sell fresh produce, as part of efforts to grow food using clean energy and indoor systems. The Crunchbase text says it is turning food production on its head to produce better food. Customers are retailers and food service buyers in the UK. Little brand awareness; the funding record is in 2024.

ImmuneOnco Biopharmaceuticals is a Shanghai-based Chinese biotech, listed in Hong Kong (1541), developing tumour immunotherapy antibodies, including the CD47-targeted IMM01 (timdarpacept) and IMM2510, a bispecific antibody. It has no marketed products and earns collaboration revenue. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

IMPACT Therapeutics is a Nanjing-based Chinese clinical-stage pharmaceutical company developing oncology drugs, led by senaparib, a PARP inhibitor for ovarian cancer, and other targeted therapies, with trials in China and the US. It is listed in Hong Kong and raised funds in 2024. Pre-commercial or early-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Inflammatix is a Sunnyvale, California diagnostics company that developed TriVerity, a blood test run on the Myrna device that reads the body's immune response in about 30 minutes to tell whether a patient has a bacterial or viral infection and how severe it is, to guide antibiotic use in emergency departments. It is venture-backed. B2B medtech with no consumer profile.

KD Pharma Group is a Swiss-based manufacturer of highly concentrated omega-3 active pharmaceutical ingredients, fish oil derivatives and related nutritional ingredients, with plants in Germany, Norway and Switzerland and sales to pharmaceutical and nutrition companies globally. Headquartered in Bioggio, Ticino. Revenue comes from supplying ingredients to drug and supplement makers. B2B manufacturer with no consumer brand.

Mithra Pharmaceuticals was a Liege, Belgium women's health company, listed on Euronext Brussels, which developed Estelle, a contraceptive combining estetrol with drospirenone, and Donesta for menopause, using estetrol (E4) produced from plants. Estelle was licensed to Gedeon Richter and Mayne Pharma. It entered bankruptcy proceedings in 2024 and its assets were sold. Pharma brand with no consumer profile.

MycoWorks is an Emeryville, California biomaterials company that grows Fine Mycelium into Reishi, a leather-like material for fashion and automotive uses, without animal hides or plastic, at a plant in South Carolina. Customers include luxury brands such as Hermes, which used the material in a bag, and automotive partners. Venture-backed. B2B materials supplier with strong luxury and sustainability interest.

NantBio is a Culver City, California biopharmaceutical company in the NantWorks family founded by Patrick Soon-Shiong, developing cancer immunotherapies, vaccines and personalised treatments that combine genomics, cell therapy and molecular engineering. It works alongside sister businesses such as ImmunityBio and NantHealth. Privately held with a large funding round in 2024. B2B developer with limited public brand awareness.

Orum Therapeutics is a Daejeon, South Korea biotech developing degrader-antibody conjugates (DACs), which join an antibody to a protein degrader to eliminate cancer targets, with lead candidate ORM-6151 for acute myeloid leukaemia and a US subsidiary. Private and venture-backed, with a funding round in December 2025. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Oxurion is a Leuven, Belgian biotech, formerly ThromboGenics and listed on Euronext Brussels, which developed treatments for diabetic eye diseases, including THR-149 for diabetic macular oedema, and sold Jetrea for vitreomacular traction. After trial setbacks it ran out of money and went bankrupt in 2024. Pharma-sector brand with no consumer profile.

Panacea Biotec is a New Delhi-based Indian biotech and pharmaceutical company, listed on the NSE and BSE, producing vaccines (such as the pentavalent and polio vaccines, including WHO-prequalified products), pharmaceutical formulations, and biosimilars for India and emerging markets. Founded in 1984. Customers include governments and UNICEF programmes. B2B and healthcare brand known in vaccines circles and to Indian doctors.

Pheon Therapeutics is a London-based clinical-stage biotech developing antibody-drug conjugates for cancer, with lead candidate PHN-010 targeting CDH6 for ovarian and kidney cancers. It was formed in 2021 with backing from Novartis Venture Fund and Atlas Venture and is venture-funded. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

PolyPid is a Petah Tikva, Israeli biotech listed on Nasdaq (PYPD) developing D-PLEX100, a drug-delivery product that releases antibiotic at the surgical site over weeks to prevent surgical site infections after abdominal surgery. It has no marketed products and is funded by equity raises. Pre-commercial B2B medtech and pharma firm with no consumer profile.

RockYou is an Oakland, California interactive media company that originally built widgets, slideshows and games for social networks such as MySpace and Facebook, then moved into social games and mobile apps, and ad technology. It was a notable early social gaming company and was hit by a 2009 data breach. Revenue comes from advertising and in-app purchases. Moderate historical consumer recognition among early Facebook users.

Sage Intacct is a San Jose, California cloud financial management and accounting software company for mid-sized businesses and non-profits, with industry-specific modules for accounting, billing, purchasing and reporting, sold by subscription. Founded in 1999 as Intacct, it was acquired by Sage Group in 2017 for about 850 million dollars. It has thousands of customers. B2B software brand known to finance teams and accountants.

Shinobi Therapeutics is a South San Francisco biotech working on engineered cell therapies made from induced pluripotent stem cells, aiming to produce off-the-shelf immune cells for cancer and other diseases. It is private and venture-backed, with a 2024 funding round. Pre-commercial B2B developer with no consumer profile.

Sound Agriculture is an Emeryville, California agricultural biotechnology company, using molecular discovery to develop small-molecule crop products, such as SOURCE, a rice yield enhancer that helps plants take up nutrients, sold to growers in California and the Southern US. It is venture-backed and works with growers directly. B2B agtech brand known to farmers and agronomists with no consumer profile.

SPR Therapeutics is a Cleveland, Ohio medical device company that makes the SPRINT peripheral nerve stimulation system, a small wearable device with a thin lead that treats chronic and acute pain without opioids, used in clinics for back, shoulder and knee pain. It sells to pain clinics and physical medicine providers and is venture-backed. B2B medtech brand with strong recognition among pain specialists.

Sudo Biosciences is a Carmel, Indiana and San Diego biotech developing selective inhibitors of the pseudokinase protein TYK2 for inflammatory and immune diseases, including topical and oral candidates for psoriasis and atopic dermatitis. It is venture-backed and pre-commercial. B2B developer with no consumer profile.

TMRW Life Sciences is a New York company that provides an automated cryostorage platform for IVF clinics and egg banks, with RFID tracking and digital monitoring of frozen eggs, embryos and sperm in the TMRW Platform. It sells to fertility clinics under storage subscriptions and is venture-backed. B2B healthcare brand with growing recognition among fertility providers and patients.
